value.name: Lucia accuses him of firing the housekeeper
value.description: Lucia confronts the man about ending the housekeeper's employment.

value.name: He defends giving notice after the house sale
value.description: He explains that he did not fire the housekeeper outright, but gave notice and severance because the house is being sold.
evidence: "I didn't fire her. I told her we couldn't keep her on once the house sold. Which it is going to. I gave her notice. I gave her severance. I —"

value.name: Lucia objects to the timing of the notice
value.description: Lucia points out that the housekeeper was given notice the day after the funeral, implying insensitivity.
evidence: "You gave her notice the day after the funeral."

value.name: They argue over keeping payroll for the empty house
value.description: He insists there is no reason to keep paying staff for a house no one will live in, while Lucia challenges his unilateral decision-making.
evidence: "What was I supposed to do, Lucia, keep her on payroll for a house no one is going to live in?"
"It's exactly half my decision, according to the will you keep waving around."

value.name: Asha interrupts the argument
value.description: Asha quietly tells them to stop, and the room falls silent.
evidence: Asha said the word quietly, and they both stopped,

value.name: Asha asserts control over the sale decision
value.description: Asha announces that they will not accept the offer that day and frames the refusal as a probate precaution.
evidence: "Here is what we are going to do," she said. "We are not going to accept the offer today."

value.name: Asha explains probate risk from closing too soon
value.description: Asha warns that closing before confirming the governing document could cloud title and expose both the estate and the executor.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano, before you respond, please understand I am not refusing on your sister's behalf. I am refusing on the estate's behalf, because as the attorney handling probate I cannot in good conscience let you close on the sale of the principal asset until I have satisfied myself that the document governing that asset is the operative one. If a later instrument exists, and it changes the disposition of the house, and we close before it surfaces, the buyer's title is clouded, the estate is exposed, and you personally as executor are exposed. Do you understand what I am telling you."

value.name: Mr. Serrano denies any later instrument exists
value.description: Mr. Serrano insists that no later document changing the house's disposition exists.

value.name: Asha requests time to verify the documents
value.description: Asha says that confirming the paperwork would only cost a few days.
evidence: "Then helping me confirm that costs you nothing but a few days."

value.name: Mr. Serrano says time is running out
value.description: Mr. Serrano rejects the delay, saying they do not have a few days.
